knowledge:
- key_parameters: filter=If TRUE, drops repeated/artifact features with similarity > 0.99 and equal m/z, retention time, and max intensity ;; mzerror=Relative error parameter for m/z when filtering repeated features ;; rtdiff=Retention time difference parameter for filtering repeated features ;; intdiff=Intensity difference parameter for filtering repeated features ;; ppm=Defines the range of accepted relative error in ppm units for isotope and adduct matching ;; adinfo=Data frame containing the list of possible adducts (e.g., positive.adinfo or negative.adinfo) ;; polarity=Set to "positive" or "negative" depending on the ionization mode ;; normalizeScore=If TRUE, normalizes scores to a 0-100 scale to allow comparison across different annotation groups ;; topmasstotal=Controls the number of top-scoring neutral masses selected per clique to speed up computation ;; topmassf=Controls the number of top-scoring neutral masses selected per feature to speed up computation ;; sizeanG=Defines the size threshold of a "big" clique for splitting annotation groups
- alternatives: None mentioned
- when_to_use: When processing untargeted LC/MS metabolomics data to group coeluting features, annotate isotopes, and identify adducts/fragments to obtain neutral metabolite masses.
- pitfalls: Duplicate artifact features can be produced by peak-picking algorithms; use filter = TRUE in getCliques to remove them ;; Scoring all annotations in large cliques can be computationally expensive; use topmasstotal, topmassf, and sizeanG to optimize speed ;; Raw scores are size-dependent and cannot be compared across different annotation groups; set normalizeScore = TRUE for comparable scores.

workflows.name: lcms_feature_annotation
workflows.intent: Group coeluting LC/MS features into cliques, annotate isotopes, and identify adducts/fragments to obtain neutral metabolite masses.
input: standards.mzXML (raw LC/MS data file in mzXML format)
workflows.stages: 1. Read and process raw LC/MS data using xcms to find chromatographic peaks ;; 2. Create an anClique S4 object from the processed peak data ;; 3. Group coeluting features into cliques using getCliques ;; 4. Annotate isotopes within each clique group using getIsotopes ;; 5. Annotate adducts and fragments using getAnnotation with an adduct information list ;; 6. Extract the annotated peak list and clique groups
workflows.code:
library(cliqueMS)
mzfile <- system.file("standards.mzXML", package = "cliqueMS")
library(xcms)
mzraw <- MSnbase::readMSData(files = mzfile, mode = "onDisk")
cpw <- CentWaveParam(ppm = 15, peakwidth = c(5,20), snthresh = 10)
mzData <- findChromPeaks(object = mzraw, param = cpw)
ex.anClique <- createanClique(mzData)
set.seed(2)
ex.cliqueGroups <- getCliques(mzData, filter = TRUE)
ex.Isotopes <- getIsotopes(ex.cliqueGroups, ppm = 10)
data(positive.adinfo)
head(positive.adinfo)
data(negative.adinfo)
head(negative.adinfo)
ex.Adducts <- getAnnotation(ex.Isotopes, ppm = 10,
    adinfo = positive.adinfo, polarity = "positive",
    normalizeScore = TRUE)
features.clique6 <- getlistofCliques(ex.Adducts)[[6]]
head(getPeaklistanClique(ex.Adducts)[features.clique6,
    c("an1","mass1","an2", "mass2", "an3", "mass3", "an4", "mass4", "an5",
    "mass5")], n = 10)
